limits: durationMs <= 10000, faults <= 30, inspect output <= 60 lines
fault actions (faults: [{atMs, action, args}]):
  partition {"groups":[["n1","n2"],["n3","n4","n5"]]}: split the network into groups; messages between groups are dropped, including in-flight ones
  isolate {"node":"n1"}: cut one node off from all others
  heal {}: remove every partition
  crash {"node":"n1"}: crash a node: volatile state is lost, whatever it persisted to disk survives
  restart {"node":"n1"}: restart a crashed node from its disk
  pause {"node":"n1","durationMs":400}: freeze a node (GC-style): it processes nothing, messages queue and timers fire late, then it resumes
  setNetwork {"minLatencyMs":1,"maxLatencyMs":80,"dropRate":0.1,"duplicateRate":0.05}: change the network model from this time on; every field is optional
workload: each client process has at most one outstanding op; ops are reads and writes on keys x, y, z, ...; write values are unique per key. Clients follow leader hints and retry. An op that times out is indeterminate (status info) and its process retires; status fail means the op definitely did not take effect.
checker: per-key linearizability of the recorded history; verdict ok, violation or unknown (checker timeout).

input.summary:
I found no linearizability violation in target-d after 20 experiments, and I don't think it has an easily reachable bug. Every run came back "ok".

What I tried, mostly with seed 42 plus a few other seeds:
- Isolating the leader, with reads sent to the leader and to any node.
- Pausing the leader to create a zombie leader. I also paused several nodes at once and paused leaders repeatedly.
- Partitioning into 2/3 splits, with the leader in the minority, and flapping partitions with heals.
- Crashing and restarting single nodes, rapid crash/restart cycles on every node, and a full-cluster crash followed by restart.
- Lossy, duplicating and high-latency networks, with drop rates up to 25%, duplicate rates up to 50% and latency up to 120 ms.
- Short client timeouts, 1 to 3 keys, 4 to 10 clients, and runs up to 10 s.

Old leaders stepped down on heal, and no stale or lost reads showed up. Reads sent to any node were also linearizable. A violation may still exist under timing I didn't hit, so this is a negative result, not proof the system is correct.
